entries.title: Proverbs 27:1
segments: ¶Boast not thyself of to-morrow, for thou knowest not what a day will bring forth.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:2
segments: ¶Let another praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:3
segments: ¶A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's vexation is heavier than them both.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:4
segments: Fury is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

entries.title: Proverbs 27:5
segments: ¶Open rebuke is better than hidden love.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:6
segments: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:7
segments: ¶The full soul trampleth on a honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:8
segments: ¶As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:9
segments: ¶Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart; and the sweetness of one's friend is [the fruit] of hearty counsel.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:10
segments: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; and go not into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:11
segments: ¶Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, that I may have wherewith to answer him that reproacheth me.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:12
segments: ¶A prudent [man] seeth the evil, [and] hideth himself; the simple pass on, [and] are punished.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:13
segments: ¶Take his garment that is become surety [for] another, and hold him in pledge for a strange woman.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:14
segments: ¶He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be reckoned a curse to him.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:15
segments: ¶A continual dropping on a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike:

entries.title: Proverbs 27:16
segments: whosoever will restrain her restraineth the wind, and his right hand encountereth oil.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:17
segments: ¶Iron is sharpened by iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:18
segments: ¶Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; and he that guardeth his master shall be honoured.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:19
segments: ¶As [in] water face [answereth] to face, so the heart of man to man.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:20
segments: ¶Sheol and destruction are insatiable; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:21
segments: ¶The fining-pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; so let a man be to the mouth that praiseth him.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:22
segments: ¶If thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his folly depart from him.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:23
segments: ¶Be well acquainted with the appearance of thy flocks; look well to thy herds:

entries.title: Proverbs 27:24
segments: for wealth is not for ever; and doth the crown [endure] from generation to generation?

entries.title: Proverbs 27:25
segments: The hay is removed, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered in.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:26
segments: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of a field;

entries.title: Proverbs 27:27
segments: and there is goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and sustenance for thy maidens.
